dedupe_keys.name: geospatial inventory of critical coastal infrastructure in the caribbean

description: This dataset is a standardised GIS inventory of coastal critical infrastructure facilities in the Caribbean, namely seaports, airports, energy facilities and wastewater facilities, with their assets such as buildings digitised as polygons. It was created by Austin Becker, Noah Hallisey and Gerald Bove, published on DesignSafe-CI in 2023 with a methodology for identifying, inventorying and quantifying infrastructure at risk from hurricanes and sea-level rise. Features were digitised from ESRI World Imagery of 2015 to 2020, giving facility and asset level detail across the region's islands. Access: download from DesignSafe project PRJ-4080. Licence: terms are shown on the DesignSafe project page (the DataCite record lists none); free. Caveats: imagery dates vary by site, facilities were identified visually, and later construction is not captured. Simulation uses: exposure of ports, airports and utility sites to storm surge and sea-level rise, land-use change tracking and prioritising adaptation. Related records: the Critical Infrastructure Spatial Index and the Onslow community resilience testbed.
